steps.title: Look at the sentences again.
steps.sub: love catching · keen on swimming · into watching
steps.prompt: What form comes after love, enjoy, don’t mind and can’t stand?
steps.answer: verb + -ing
steps.why: These verbs and phrases are followed by the -ing form: I love walking, not I love to walk in this pattern.

steps.title: Saying how much you like something
steps.html:
FeelingExpressionExample
↑↑love / really likeI love walking in the mountains.
↑like / enjoyI enjoy watching the first snowfall.
→don’t mindI don’t mind getting wet.
↓am not keen onI’m not keen on swimming in the sea.
↓↓can’t stand / hateI can’t stand sitting indoors all afternoon.

All of these are followed by a verb in the -ing form, or by a noun: I love walking / I love the mountains.

Don’t mind means “it is not a problem for me” — it is not the same as “I like it”.

Can’t stand is stronger than don’t like. It means you really hate it.

Spelling of the -ing form: walk → walking, get → getting (double the consonant), make → making (drop the e).

The -ing form comes back as a full topic in Unit 10, Lesson 28.

steps.title: Web post · model
steps.html:
A web post recommending when to visit a country. You will write your own at the end.

When to come to Kazakhstan — and when to stay at home

If you ask me when to visit my country, I will say May. The best time to come is the second half of May, when the steppe is green and the days are long and pleasant.

I love walking in the mountains near Almaty in spring, and I don’t mind getting wet, because the rain never lasts. In May the light is soft, the parks are full, and the apple trees are in flower. It’s worth staying a few days in the city and then going up to Big Almaty Lake.

Avoid July and August if you can’t stand sitting indoors all afternoon. In some periods the temperature stays above 35 degrees for a week. Those afternoons are hot, humid and uncomfortable, and most people I know go out only in the evening.

Winter is a different country. I enjoy watching the first snowfall in November, but January is cold, damp and cloudy for weeks. Don’t miss the Nauryz festival on 22 March if you like crowds: it is the one day when the whole city is outside.

So: come in May, stay for the food, and leave the heat to us.

items.text: The best time to come is …

steps.title: Write your own web post: the best time to visit your city or country.
steps.sub: About 120–160 words. Follow the five paragraphs of the model.
steps.placeholder: The best time to come is …
steps.html:
1. Plan (from the model): 1 when to come → 2 what to do then → 3 when to stay away → 4 one season and one festival → 5 one short final line.
  • 1 The best time to come is …
  • 2 I love …ing … It’s worth …
  • 3 Avoid … if you can’t stand …ing
  • 4 Don’t miss …
  • 5 So: …
The best time to come isIt’s worthAvoidDon’t missI loveI enjoyI don’t mindI can’t standpleasanthumiddampcloudysnowfallfestivalseason
steps.modelHtml:
• I used all four phrases from the Useful language box.
  • I used at least three of: love / enjoy / don’t mind / can’t stand.
  • Every one of them is followed by an -ing form or a noun.
  • I wrote about a time to avoid, not only the good months.
  • I used at least four weather words from this lesson.
